title: T1586.001 — Compromise Accounts - Social Media Accounts
subtitle: The story below shows one full attack in eight steps: a fake login page, one typed password, a hijacked company LinkedIn page, and the defender view at every moment.
aria: Animated diagram: attackers phish a marketing manager, harvest the SSO password, take over the company social media page, and the SOC responds. A full text version follows in the written steps below.

steps.title: Set up the trap
steps.caption: The attacker stands up a fake single sign-on login page. The page is a copy of the real one and saves every typed password.
steps.defender: Nothing in company logs yet. The fake page lives on attacker infrastructure.

detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Send the lure
steps.caption: The attacker sends a message: your company LinkedIn page was flagged, sign in to appeal. The manager trusts the warning.
steps.defender: If the lure arrives by work email, the email gateway sees it. Direct messages stay invisible.

steps.defender: No alert. This is the blind spot the technique abuses.

steps.defender: IdP shows a sign-in to the social media app from a new country and device.

steps.caption: The attacker changes the recovery email and starts a data export of connections. This keeps the account even if the password changes.
steps.defender: Recovery email change and data export may trigger platform emails - often noticed days later.

steps.title: Post and DM from a trusted voice
steps.caption: The attacker posts a scam offer and sends many direct messages. The message looks official because the page is real.
steps.defender: No platform logs for the company. Brand monitoring and user reports are the sensors.

steps.caption: the link and lands on a second fake login page. A second account is now at risk

steps.caption: The SOC reports the account, revokes SSO sessions, forces a password reset, and warns staff.
